claim: Post-training alignment on synthetic data yields positive average gains but does not provide a universal performance boost across real-world tasks; the effect is task-dependent and can be absent or detrimental in some settings.
falsifier: Apply the same synthetic-data alignment recipe to a suite of diverse real-world tasks and compare per-task performance against a baseline; the recipe should show positive average gains while failing or harming performance on at least some tasks.

conditions: evaluation across different real-world domains and task types
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported models, synthetic datasets, alignment methods, and evaluated tasks; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
